about.purpose: A starting palette of prompts for the ARDY core model, so the engine ships with something better than a blank box.
about.phrasing: ARDY's text encoder was trained on Bones Rigplay captions, which are third-person declarative sentences ('A person is walking.'). Prompts here follow that form. Imperative fragments ('walk to the desk', 'wave hello') are off-distribution *phrasing* even when the motion itself is in-distribution, and are more likely to drift. See README.

provenance_values.upstream_preset: Shipped by the model authors in nv-tlabs/ardy scripts/interactive_demo/common.py PRESET_PROMPTS. Author-vetted phrasing.
provenance_values.upstream_doc: Used as a worked example in nv-tlabs/ardy scripts/generate.py.
provenance_values.derived: Written for this library against the documented training distribution. In-distribution by construction, but not author-vetted.

verification.status: UNVERIFIED — no prompt in this file has been confirmed on ARDY hardware yet.
verification.how: Run scripts/validate_prompts.py on the ARDY host against a live Director service, then --write-back to fold the results into the 'verified' and 'observed' fields.
verification.why_it_matters: 'verified': false means nobody has watched this prompt produce motion. Do not read the notes as observations; they are expectations.

categories.locomotion: Ground travel: walk, run, side-step, direction and style variations.
categories.turning: Changing facing, in place or while moving.
categories.ground_transitions: Sit, stand, crouch, bow — vertical transitions of the whole body.
categories.idle: Low-energy standing behaviour — useful as filler between beats.
categories.out_of_distribution: Documented failures. These are NOT recommended prompts; they are here so users know the model's edges and are not surprised.

prompts.prompt: A person is walking.
prompts.note: The canonical baseline. Upstream ships it as the demo's default prompt; if this one misbehaves, suspect the setup, not the prompt.

prompts.prompt: A person is walking backwards.
prompts.note: Travels opposite the facing direction, so root displacement is negative along the heading axis.

prompts.prompt: A person side steps to the right.
prompts.note: Lateral travel with facing held. Useful for staging without changing which way the character looks.

prompts.prompt: A person side steps to the left.
prompts.note: Mirror of the upstream right-side preset. Worth checking whether left/right asymmetry shows up in the dataset.

prompts.prompt: A person is running forward.
prompts.note: Higher root speed than walking; expect a flight phase, so foot-contact fraction should drop well below the walk baseline.

prompts.prompt: A person walks forward slowly.
prompts.note: Speed adverb test. If displacement matches the plain walk, the model is ignoring the adverb — worth knowing.

prompts.prompt: A young lady walks forward elegantly.
prompts.note: Shows the encoder responds to style and subject wording, not just the verb.

prompts.prompt: A person walks in a circle.
prompts.note: Upstream's own generate.py example. Needs a long duration to close the arc; at 4s you get a shallow curve instead.

prompts.prompt: A person turns around and walks back.
prompts.note: Two beats in one prompt. Compare against splitting it across /choreograph steps — this is the cheapest test of which approach reads better.

prompts.prompt: A person turns to the left while walking.
prompts.note: Curved path rather than a pivot. Ends on a different heading, which matters when chaining steps.

prompts.prompt: A person makes a sharp right turn.
prompts.note: Tests whether 'sharp' tightens the arc versus the gradual turn above.

prompts.prompt: A person pivots in place to face the opposite direction.
prompts.note: Heading changes ~180 degrees with little root travel. The one to use when staging a character who must face the other way without moving.

prompts.prompt: A person is standing.
prompts.note: The rest pose. Handy as a neutral opening or closing beat in a choreography.

prompts.prompt: A person sits down.
prompts.note: No chair exists in the scene — the model only knows the body motion, so the character sits on nothing. Stage a prop yourself if you need one.

prompts.prompt: A person stands up from sitting.
prompts.note: Starts from a seated pose the model has to assume on its own; the first frames may snap. Chaining it after 'sits down' should read better than running it cold.

prompts.prompt: A person bows down and then stands upright.
prompts.note: A complete two-beat arc in one prompt — evidence the model handles 'X then Y' within a single clip.

prompts.prompt: A person crouches down low.
prompts.note: Root height drops without a full sit.

prompts.prompt: A person jumps backwards.
prompts.note: Short and punchy; padding the duration past the jump leaves the character idling afterwards.

prompts.prompt: A person jumps.
prompts.note: Upstream's generate.py example. Vertical hop in place, so little XZ travel.

prompts.prompt: A person jumps forward.
prompts.note: A broad jump; direction comes from the prompt, distance is the model's choice.

prompts.prompt: A person hops on one leg.
prompts.note: Asymmetric contact. A good stress test of the foot-contact post-processing.

prompts.prompt: A person waves with their right hand.
prompts.note: The default 'greeting' beat. Note the phrasing: the README's 'wave hello' is the same motion in off-distribution wording.

prompts.prompt: A person raises both arms above their head.
prompts.note: Symmetric upper-body reach with the lower body still.

prompts.prompt: A person claps their hands.
prompts.note: Small-amplitude and repetitive. Fine detail like finger contact is beyond a 27-joint skeleton, so judge the arms, not the hands.

prompts.prompt: A person points forward with their right arm.
prompts.note: Directional gesture; the arm should track the facing, which makes it a decent check that heading is applied.

prompts.prompt: A person crosses their arms.
prompts.note: Static end pose rather than a cycle — the motion is the transition into it.

prompts.prompt: A person is kicking with their right leg.
prompts.note: Author-vetted. Balance is held on the support leg throughout.

prompts.prompt: A person kicks with their left leg.
prompts.note: Mirror of the upstream preset — pair them to probe left/right bias in the dataset.

prompts.prompt: A person throws a punch with their right arm.
prompts.note: Fast upper-body strike; short duration keeps it from looping into shadow-boxing.

prompts.prompt: A ballet dancer, performs a forward, turn joining feet, in a repeating loop
prompts.note: Verbatim from upstream, comma splices and all — the phrasing is odd but author-vetted, so do not 'fix' it without re-checking. 'Repeating loop' wants a long duration.

prompts.prompt: A person dances happily in place.
prompts.note: Open-ended: 'dance' spans a lot of the dataset, so expect variety across seeds. Pin the seed if you need it reproducible.

prompts.prompt: A person spins around gracefully.
prompts.note: Continuous heading change in place. Chaining after this is where carried heading matters most.

prompts.prompt: a performer gives high bow, with arms to the side, right leg crossed behind the left
prompts.note: The most specific prompt upstream ships — limb-by-limb detail. The upper bound on how much articulation the encoder actually honours.

prompts.prompt: A person stands still and looks around.
prompts.note: Filler between beats so a character is not frozen. The 27-joint core skeleton has limited head articulation, so this reads mostly as torso.

prompts.prompt: A person shifts their weight from foot to foot while standing.
prompts.note: Subtle idle with alternating foot contacts, and much less dead than plain 'standing'.

prompts.prompt: A person stretches their arms while standing.
prompts.note: Slow upper-body idle.

prompts.prompt: A person flies like superman.
prompts.note: The documented collapse case: no flight in a ground-motion dataset, so it lands on the nearest learned motion — a skip or a leap. Named in this repo's README; included so the failure is demonstrable rather than folklore.

prompts.prompt: A person swims across a pool.
prompts.note: Prone motion with no ground contact. Bones Rigplay is ground motion, so expect an upright walk with arm flailing.

prompts.prompt: A person climbs a ladder.
prompts.note: Needs vertical translation and a prop to grip. Expect stepping in place with raised arms.

prompts.prompt: A person rides a bicycle.
prompts.note: Prop-dependent, and the seated-pedalling pose has no ground-contact analogue.

prompts.prompt: Two people shake hands with each other.
prompts.note: A structural limit rather than a data gap: one model call generates one character. The second person cannot appear at any duration or seed.
